title: Refresh interactive component patterns and assemble VPAT evidence package
creator: Priya Nair
description: Scope: Audit and remediate interactive patterns across buttons, compact/virtualized tables, interactive charts, and modal/dialog flows to meet VPAT evidence needs. Deliver a consolidated VPAT artefact and a migration plan for color/contrast token updates. This ticket covers: 1) defining accessible keyboard/aria patterns for complex components (virtualized rows, stacked modals, chart legend navigation), 2) verifying and updating contrast tokens and color-vision-safe palettes, 3) producing testable examples and automated checks, and 4) assembling VPAT evidence (design specs, test matrix, QA scripts, and screenreader recordings). Out of scope: platform runtime changes to rendering engine (separate ENG ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Design specs exist for keyboard-first interaction for virtualized tables including aria-activedescendant example and programmatic focus restoration
Chart interaction pattern document with keyboard traversal of legend, series toggles, and focus order for SVG/canvas charts
Modal/stacking guidance updated to prevent focus loss and to document trap/untrap heuristics for nested dialogs
Contrast token migration plan with a tested color-vision-safe palette and token mapping (old->new) and automated visual diff snapshots
VPAT evidence package produced: conformance table, representative screenshots, voiceover/JAWS recordings, Axe/pa11y run results, and a short audit narrative
Unit and integration test checklist added to repo with CI gating for critical accessibility regressions
Design review sign-off from PM and Eng accessibility reviewer and handoff checklist for implementation

Run color contrast sweep across token set, generate visual diff snapshots, propose new token mappings (Design Tokens working group)
Write VPAT narrative and assemble artifacts (screenshots, recordings, test logs) - due before release candidate
Coordinate engineering PRs for implementation and CI accessibility checks - reference github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pulls
Perform cross-browser screen reader walkthrough and collect recordings (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS)
decisions: Adopt aria-activedescendant for virtualized table row focus to avoid DOM focus churn
Use a neutral-ish, color-vision-friendly contrast ramp and keep legacy tokens mapped for two releases to ease migration
Document modal stacking as a single focus-trap instance with explicit inertness for background content instead of multiple nested traps
